A1.justification: Despite the new Loc² title, both PDFs describe the same research, authors, matching pipeline and core experiments. Both main texts and complete appendices are readable, including equations, tables and figures, and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original KITTI and VIGOR localization experiments, design ablations, depth-robustness tests, relative-depth training results and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds KITTI orientation scenarios, CVACT transfer examples, extensive ablations and correspondence-inlier analyses.

M1.justification: The adopted pipeline retains frozen DINOv2 features, projection heads, dustbin/dual-softmax matching, depth lifting, scale-aware Procrustes alignment and VCE/InfoNCE supervision. RANSAC was already used in v1. The newly evaluated BEV-matching and homography variants are ablation controls; the proposed method itself is unchanged.

E1.justification: V3 retains KITTI and VIGOR and adds direct VIGOR-to-CVACT transfer, evaluated qualitatively on Australian scenes. It also adds fully unknown-orientation KITTI testing with ±180° noise and a non-road-facing KITTI subset. These extend geographical coverage and viewing conditions beyond v1.

E2.justification: SliceMatch, already compared on VIGOR in v1, is newly included in KITTI's ±180° comparisons in v3 Table 1. Table 12 adds BEV-matching and homography-estimation alternatives. The original KITTI comparator set remains in the ±10° block, and VIGOR's external baseline membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include uniform ±180° orientation noise during KITTI training/testing, manually selected non-road-facing evaluation, and qualitative CVACT transfer without retraining. Appendix A separately varies training and inference settings, including 256–2048 correspondences, aerial grids, image/feature resolution and temperature. These substantially extend evaluation design while retaining the original splits and core metrics.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained topmost-point, scale and depth-robustness studies, v3 tests correspondence density, resolution, temperature and RANSAC sensitivity. It directly tests BEV matching and homography alternatives, adds inlier-versus-error diagnostics, investigates road-alignment bias, and expands failure analysis with building-occlusion examples. These address substantially more robustness and design questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V3's inlier-quantile/error curves add a diagnostic analysis, without introducing uncertainty estimation or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive numerical and qualitative results, including KITTI ±180° mean localization errors of 11.71 m cross-area and 1.85 m same-area. Existing KITTI entries also change: the proposed method's cross-area mean becomes 5.60 m instead of 5.51 m, and FG2's becomes 7.31 m instead of 7.45 m. The updates are unexplained, and v1 does not specify orientation noise, so controlled performance changes cannot be inferred. Most VIGOR scores persist, although the unknown-orientation Ours-Unik3Drel row is removed.

T1.justification: V3 explicitly assumes that the camera viewing direction is orthogonal to gravity in Section 3.2, adding a stated geometric condition absent from v1. The Procrustes derivations and loss formulas remain substantively unchanged. V1's separate assumptions paragraph is removed, while similarity-transform applicability is discussed in v3 Appendix I.

C1.justification: The central claims about weakly supervised, interpretable localization and scale recovery remain. V3 adds specific headline claims that correspondence inliers and ground-layout alignment indicate localization reliability and support error detection. The introduction's explicit 26% KITTI improvement claim is removed.

C2.justification: V3 replaces v1's characterization of aerial imagery as often not orthorectified with a standard-DOM versus true-DOM discussion, proposing contextual features and confidence sampling as mitigation mechanisms. It adds explanations for homography, resolution and non-road results and interprets inliers/layout alignment as reliability signals. Conversely, v1's explicit depth-error limitation and warning that an incorrect symmetric pose can still align convincingly are omitted.

D1.justification: V3 adds a repository link and a reproducibility statement promising code, configurations and evaluation scripts; actual availability cannot be established from the PDFs. Newly disclosed details include 630×630 aerial inputs, 45×45 DINO features and three correspondences per RANSAC trial. Core optimizer, hardware, batch-size and loss settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 removes the standalone monocular-depth survey and much of the visual-grounding and LiDAR context, substantially narrowing the related-work coverage. It introduces positioning against MAST3R/VGGT-style image matching and references for CVACT and GeoCalib. The central comparison with FG2 remains; its publication metadata update does not constitute a new work.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the method Loc², v3 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction and conclusion, separates local matching from pose estimation, and recasts the qualitative narrative around interpretability. The appendices are extensively reorganized, references move before them, and dedicated limitations/broader-impact sections give way to different discussion and disclosure sections.

P2.justification: V3 redraws Figures 1–2, reorganizes qualitative panels, restructures KITTI Table 1 by orientation setting and reverses area/orientation ordering in VIGOR Table 2. It adds inlier-error and CVACT figures, ablation tables and a runtime/memory table. Earlier initial-versus-recovered-scale grids are replaced by selected layout-alignment displays.

improvement.justification: V3's controlled BEV-matching and homography comparisons directly test central design advantages that v1 largely motivated conceptually. The broader orientation tests, sensitivity studies and inlier-error analysis substantially strengthen the empirical support for the method. CVACT evidence remains qualitative, and removing useful symmetry/depth-error caveats weakens qualification, but the added controls and diagnostic evidence provide a substantial net improvement.
